subject: Dieux Skin
method: CO0 final pre-Phase-2 consolidation of the terminal CO1, CO2, and CO3 returns. Closely overlapping provisional community axes were merged only where they described the same decision tension; service evidence was added as a separate material axis because it changes buying confidence but cannot support product-performance claims. Material Axis Discovery Closure then re-audited every admitted source-native unit under an open taxonomy, terminally dispositioned each new candidate, and required two later diverse dry probes.

axes.label: Hydration, barrier support, and visible results
axes.scope: Instant Angel, Air Angel, Skin Mercy, Deliverance, and brand-level performance
axes.customer_tension: Customers report durable hydration and barrier comfort, but also insufficient moisture or unclear visible effect under some conditions.
axes.segment_or_condition: Dry or dehydrated skin, seasonal dryness, damaged barriers, and users seeking redness or visible-change benefits.
axes.strongest_counterevidence: Repeated repurchase and editorial use tests describe sustained hydration, comfort, and reduced redness in bounded individual conditions.
axes.known_gap: Search must test whether favorable and unfavorable outcomes segment by product, skin state, climate, or routine rather than treating hydration as one brand-wide effect.

axes.label: Irritation, breakout, and active/post-procedure fit
axes.scope: Reaction risk and condition-dependent compatibility across Deliverance and moisturizers
axes.customer_tension: Some users describe irritation, breakouts, or niacinamide intolerance while others report calm, redness reduction, or post-active compatibility.
axes.segment_or_condition: Sensitive, acne-prone, rosacea-prone, retinoid-using, post-procedure, and niacinamide-sensitive users.
axes.strongest_counterevidence: Source-native editorial and community accounts report reduced redness and comfortable use when the person tolerates the formula and matches it to condition.
axes.known_gap: Search must test condition and ingredient-tolerance segmentation without converting anecdotes into medical-safety or efficacy claims.

axes.label: Texture, finish, sensory acceptability, makeup, and routine compatibility
axes.scope: Weight, richness, pilling, layering, odor or scent acceptability, perceived product integrity, makeup wear, and day/night or seasonal fit
axes.customer_tension: The same richness and unfragranced formula that can read as cushioning or gentle can feel greasy, heavy, pill under makeup, or carry a musty, sour, glue-like, or otherwise unacceptable odor that changes use, return, or repurchase behavior.
axes.segment_or_condition: Oily versus dry skin, humid versus cold climates, makeup wearers, scent-sensitive users, and people distinguishing expected unfragranced odor from suspected spoilage.
axes.strongest_counterevidence: Some customers describe the formula as neutral or pleasantly unscented, while others explicitly accept a transient odor because the hydration or finish is valuable.
axes.known_gap: Keep product, batch, sensory tolerance, climate, and routine fit separate; odor reports do not establish contamination, spoilage, or population prevalence.

axes.label: Packaging, dispensing, and reusable use-cycle usability
axes.scope: Pumps, tubes, caps, leakage, access to remaining product, product loss, and reusable accessory adhesion, serum compatibility, cleaning, drying, storage, durability, and waste reduction
axes.customer_tension: A package can waste or obstruct an otherwise liked formula, while a reusable accessory can create real utility through adhesion, serum flexibility, easy cleaning, and reduced waste—or lose value through drying, storage, durability, or repeated-use friction.
axes.segment_or_condition: Repeat purchasers, travelers, users judging usable quantity, and reusable-eye-mask buyers evaluating adhesion, cleaning, drying, storage, durability, and serum compatibility.
axes.strongest_counterevidence: Many product-positive accounts do not mention package failure, and multiple Forever Eye Mask reviews describe secure adhesion, easy rinsing, flexible serum pairing, and reduced disposable waste.
axes.known_gap: Keep container failure separate from reusable-accessory utility and test product/version specificity without treating captured review incidence as prevalence.

axes.label: Price, value, hype, and product trust
axes.scope: Prestige price, usable quantity, repeat-purchase economics, dupe/replacement logic, and confidence in product claims
axes.customer_tension: Customers can value formula feel and results while still rejecting the price, quantity, or hype-to-difference gap.
axes.segment_or_condition: Budget-sensitive repeat buyers, prestige switchers, and customers comparing adequate lower-cost substitutes.
axes.strongest_counterevidence: Some repeat buyers explicitly accept the premium for texture, luxury, or reliable personal fit; the Strategist account also says Instant Angel felt more luxurious even after switching for price.
axes.known_gap: Search must distinguish generic price complaint, actual executed switching, and cases where premium experience remains defensible.

axes.label: Segment, condition, and portfolio product fit
axes.scope: Choosing among Dieux products by skin state, climate, routine slot, and desired intensity
axes.customer_tension: The portfolio offers meaningful internal fit choices, but unclear boundaries can produce mismatch, over-richness, under-moisturizing, or selection confusion.
axes.segment_or_condition: Dry, oily, acne-prone, sensitive, mature, rosacea-prone, seasonal, and active-using customers.
axes.strongest_counterevidence: Community and editorial bodies repeatedly articulate a coherent internal ladder from lighter Air Angel through Instant Angel to repair-focused Skin Mercy.
axes.known_gap: Search must test whether the internal ladder is legible and sufficient versus customers leaving the portfolio for a more condition-specific alternative.

axes.label: Repeat purchase, rejection, and switching destinations
axes.scope: Executed customer behavior and named external or internal destinations
axes.customer_tension: Dieux earns real repeat purchase and recommendation, yet price, fit, reactions, or routine performance can drive replacement and switch-back behavior.
axes.segment_or_condition: Experienced users with direct comparative use and a stated purchase or routine consequence.
axes.strongest_counterevidence: The coded community set contains substantially more retained/repurchased rows than explicit switch rows, but those are qualitative row counts, not population incidence.
axes.known_gap: Search must distinguish true executed destinations from comparison mentions and identify which tension actually caused the move.

axes.label: Availability, fulfillment, support, returns, and buying confidence
axes.scope: Stock and geographic access, including ingredient- or regulation-driven SKU market exclusions; retailer-channel and format availability; DTC order fulfillment; shipping; order accuracy; customer support; returns/refunds; and transaction trust
axes.customer_tension: A customer can like or never reach the product yet lose confidence because it is unavailable in their market, repeatedly out of stock, delayed, mis-shipped, or poorly resolved through support or refunds.
axes.segment_or_condition: DTC purchasers, international or channel-constrained shoppers, and customers encountering stockouts, delayed or missing delivery, wrong orders, support contact, or return/refund friction.
axes.strongest_counterevidence: The official policy provides support and missing-package pathways, and retailer access can bypass some DTC friction; the captured service and availability accounts are self-selected and do not establish prevalence.
axes.known_gap: Test recurrence by channel and geography while keeping access and service evidence separate from product-performance claims.

excluded_or_merged_provisional_axes.reason: Strongest delight is a required counterweight for every material axis, not a separate customer tension.
Named destination examples sharpen the existing switching axis but do not change a competitive decision.

claim_ceiling: This inventory routes Phase 2. It is not prevalence, causation, medical-safety, market-consensus, or final axis-closure authority.

material_axis_discovery.claim_boundary: All admitted units were accounted for and two later diverse residual probes were dry; this is not universal internet exhaustion.
